title: Amplitude, wavelength and frequency on a wave diagram
examples: What is the wavelength of a wave?
How do you calculate wave speed?

figure.name: x-wave
figure.note: A wave carries energy from left to right

explain.say: Stand on a beach in Bali and watch the waves roll in. Some are tall, some are long, some come quickly one after another. Scientists use three words to describe any wave. Let us find each one on this wave.

draw.text: Amplitude, wavelength and frequency on a wave diagram

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A wave carries energy from left to right

explain.say: Look at the wavelength arrow. Wavelength is the distance from one peak to the next peak, one full wave. It is measured in metres. Can you find two peaks next to each other?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A wave carries energy from left to right

explain.say: Well spotted! Now the amplitude. Amplitude is the height from the middle line up to a peak. A bigger amplitude means more energy: a loud sound or a huge sea wave. Is amplitude from the bottom to the top?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A wave carries energy from left to right

explain.say: Not quite, it is middle to top, so half of that! Now frequency: how many waves pass a point every second. It is measured in hertz, and 1 hertz means one wave per second. If 2 waves pass you each second, what is the frequency?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A wave carries energy from left to right

explain.say: 2 hertz, great! Now the magic formula: wave speed equals frequency times wavelength. Waves 10 metres long arriving at 0.5 hertz travel at 5 metres per second. Wow fact: your ears hear from about 20 to 20 000 hertz. Challenge: what is the speed of a 2 hertz, 3 metre wave?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: A wave carries energy from left to right

faq.a: Wavelength is the distance from one point on a wave to the same point on the next wave, such as peak to peak.
asks: What is the wavelength of a wave?

faq.a: Amplitude is the largest distance a point moves from its middle, or rest, position. Bigger amplitude means more energy.
Frequency is the number of waves passing a point each second, measured in hertz.

faq.q: How do you calculate wave speed?
faq.a: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength, v equals f lambda. A 2 hertz wave with a 3 metre wavelength moves at 6 metres per second.
A wave carries energy from one place to another without carrying the material along with it.

facts: Healthy young human ears hear roughly 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz.

quiz.say: A wave has frequency 4 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
quiz.show: A wave has frequency 4 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
quiz.why: v = f × λ = 4 × 2 = 8 metres per second.

wrong.0: That divides; wave speed is frequency times wavelength.
